course_name_original: TECNOLOGIE PER L'ELABORAZIONE DEI DATI GIURIDICI Canale unico
course_name_en: TECHNOLOGIES FOR THE PROCESSING OF LEGAL DATA Single channel
prerequisites: Familiarity with the fundamental concepts of the legal system

learning_outcomes.text: Understand legal statements to proceed with correct legal qualifications. Knowledge of the principles and legal issues related to the use of digital technologies. Knowledge of blockchain technology and understanding of its applications to digital currencies and contracts. Knowledge of the fundamental principles and elements of GDPR and legal issues related to the use of Artificial Intelligence tools.

Be able to build a taxonomy within which to frame objects, relationships, and events in interactive processes from which to extract a structured set of rules for the elaboration of a legal knowledge system. Understanding of anonymity issues in the management of personal data in multiple situations.
Be able to evaluate the effectiveness and legal adequacy of technological solutions in the management of personal data.
Be able to effectively communicate problems and solutions adopted to legal experts, without technological knowledge, and to IT experts, without legal knowledge.

The course will allow the development of independent in-depth study skills on course topics or related ones. It will also allow the student to easily consult advanced and/or specific manuals for autonomous learning of legal issues concerning digital solutions.
Understand the principles of computer representation of legal knowledge, with particular reference to the formalization of concepts, relationships, and rules in criminal law.
Analyze and disambiguate legal statements, identifying the elements necessary for their structured representation.
Understand the functioning of computer systems supporting decisions in the judicial field, also through the analysis of the Daedalus P.M. Assistant system and use cases.
Know the fundamental principles of algorithmic technologies and machine learning methods and understand their use in data-driven applications.
Analyze issues related to personal data protection, anonymization, transparency, fairness, reliability, and interpretability of algorithmic systems.
Understand the main ethical and regulatory implications of digital technologies, with particular reference to GDPR and the AI Act.
Develop critical analysis skills regarding the opportunities, risks, and responsibilities associated with the use of information technologies in decision-making processes.

syllabus_topics: Computer representation of legal knowledge, with particular reference to criminal law
Analysis of criminal norms and cybercrime provisions
Structured representation of legal concepts, objects, relationships, events, and rules
Construction of taxonomies and disambiguation of legal statements
Computer systems for decision support in the judicial field
The Daedalus P.M. Assistant system: principles, functionalities, and use cases
Fundamentals of data-driven technologies, algorithms, and machine learning
Applications of algorithmic systems and social and ethical implications of automated decision-making
Anonymization and pseudonymization of data
Privacy, social networks, and personal data protection: GDPR
Bitcoin and blockchain technology
Ethical issues of artificial intelligence: biases, fairness, reliability, transparency, interpretability, and responsibility
Risks and regulation of artificial intelligence: AI Act
Introduction to the computer representation of legal knowledge
Analysis of criminal norms: general part and provisions related to cybercrime
Concepts, objects, relations, and events in the representation of law
Construction of taxonomies and structured representation of legal rules
Linguistic analysis and disambiguation of legal statements
Computer systems for decision support in the judicial field
The Daedalus P.M. Assistant system: conceptual architecture, functionalities, and represented knowledge
Analysis of use cases and exercises on the Daedalus system
Introduction to data-driven technologies and their social and ethical implications
Fundamentals of algorithms and machine learning methods
Applications of algorithmic systems and case studies in decision-making processes
Anonymization and pseudonymization of open data
Protection of personal data, social networks, and GDPR
Bitcoin and fundamental principles of blockchain technology
Ethical issues of artificial intelligence: biases, fairness, reliability, and responsibility
Transparency and interpretability of artificial intelligence systems
Risks of artificial intelligence and European regulatory framework: AI Act
assessment_rules: The assessment verifies knowledge of topics, understanding of principles and methodologies, and ability to apply them to case studies, with particular attention to linking technological, legal, and ethical aspects. The concrete verification consists of an oral exam, possibly accompanied by a project completed by the students.
